subject: Injunctive relief procedure and expedited discovery carve — MSA redlines
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@novaworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Gabriel Torres <legal@novaworks.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline: emergency relief + discovery carve

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for sending the draft. Our GC team is concerned about two narrow items we redlined:

1) Express mechanism for obtaining emergency injunctive relief in our home court (CA) without triggering a waiver of arbitration for the underlying dispute.
2) A short "expedited discovery" carve so a party can preserve critical logs/forensics while any challenge to jurisdiction or arbitral forum is resolved.

Gabriel and I attached a markup showing the language we prefer. We're not trying to block arbitration — we want a pragmatic corridor so if there is urgent data preservation (server-side logs, KV cache snapshots, billing traces) we can get immediate access while keeping the arbitration pathway for contract remedies.

Can Redwood confirm whether a limited interim-judicial-access clause is acceptable, and whether Redwood is comfortable with our proposed 7-day preservation notice window?

Appreciate quick feedback — NovaWorks is on a tight implementation timeline.

Best,
Alex

[Attachment: NovaWorks_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@novaworks.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: emergency relief + discovery carve

Alex —

Thanks — received and looping in legal. Short answers up front: we think the concept is reasonable but need tweaks to avoid effectively bypassing arbitration for all interim matters. Key internal priorities:

- Keep injunctive relief limited to "preservation and narrow injunctive relief" (no declaratory judgments).
- Tighten notice and scope so any judicial step is only for immediate preservation (logs, snapshots, account suspension).
- Define "expedited discovery" narrowly and with clear privilege-preserving procedures.

Kimberly/Karthik — can you review the attached redline and propose counter-language we can present to NovaWorks? Prefer we give them a single tracked-change proposal.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redline: emergency relief + discovery carve

Marissa / Karthik —

I reviewed NovaWorks' markup. Attached is a short playbook excerpt and a proposed replacement paragraph. Highlights:

- Proposed clause: Redwood agrees that either party may seek emergency interim relief from a court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve evidence, suspend account access, or prevent imminent and irreparable harm to tangible systems. Such relief is limited to preservation measures and shall not be construed as a waiver of any party's right to have the dispute resolved by arbitration pursuant to Section X.

- Expedited discovery: limit to preservation notices, targeted subpoenas for logs, and production of non-privileged diagnostic exports. Any compelled discovery beyond preservation requires an arbitral ruling or mutual agreement.

- Forum selection note: we propose defaulting emergency-court venue to the county/state where Redwood's corporate headquarters are located (San Francisco County, CA), but include a mutual-opt-out to specify an alternative neutral forum by written agreement before any emergency petition is filed.

I also added an explicit confidentiality protocol for handing over logs (redaction obligations, secure upload, limited distribution). See Redwood_InterimRelief_Playbook.docx (excerpt attached).

Next steps: Marissa — if you approve, I'll send the tracked-change version to NovaWorks with a short note explaining the mutual-opt-out mechanism (keeps arbitration intact while making interim relief operational).

Kimberly

[Attachment: Redwood_InterimRelief_Playbook.docx (docx)]

From: Gabriel Torres <legal@novaworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@novaworks.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Sep 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: emergency relief + discovery carve

On Mon, Sep 17, 2028 at 08:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex —
> 
> Thanks — received and looping in legal. Short answers up front: we think the concept is reasonable but need tweaks to avoid effectively bypassing arbitration for all interim matters.

Marissa / Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick review and the playbook. A few clarifications from our side before we accept your language:

1) "Court of competent jurisdiction" — we'd prefer to name "California federal courts" as the default for emergency petitions (federal enforcement tends to be faster for evidence preservation). Is Redwood comfortable with federal district (ND Cal) as the default emergency court, with an agreed mutual-opt-out?

2) Preservation notice window — we proposed 7 days. Your draft seemed to contemplate faster action. We need 7 days minimum to coordinate internal forensics and counsel. Can Redwood commit to preserving copies for that period after written notice?

3) Expedited discovery scope — we want clarity on what Redwood considers "non-privileged diagnostic exports" (examples: request_id, session timestamps, request/response digests, server error traces). Also: who performs redactions? Our preference is Redwood provides exported artifacts, and NovaWorks' counsel performs redaction under a protective order.

If we can converge on (1)-(3) we'll accept the mutual-opt-out and move forward. We're trying to avoid litigation timelines but need operational certainty for launch.

Thanks,
Gabriel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Gabriel Torres <legal@novaworks.com>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@novaworks.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline: emergency relief + discovery carve

Gabriel —

Thanks for the clear questions. Agreed approach below (I'll incorporate in a tracked-change and send a single redline):

- Default emergency court: Northern District of California (federal) for injunctive preservation petitions; parties may jointly elect an alternative forum in writing before any petition is filed.
- Preservation window: Redwood will preserve copies of requested artifacts for 7 calendar days from receipt of a written preservation notice. For time-sensitive items, Redwood will hold an initial 72-hour hold and notify NovaWorks immediately; the full 7-day preservation follows to allow counsel coordination.
- Expedited artifacts: Redwood will provide targeted diagnostic exports (request_id, timestamps, non-content digests, error traces, and billing/event counters). Redwood will not produce raw customer content or decrypted secrets.
- Redaction protocol: Redwood will produce artifacts to counsel under a mutual protective order; Redwood will perform initial technical redactions for data that cannot be segregated (e.g., embedded secrets), and NovaWorks' counsel may request further redactions which Redwood will evaluate promptly.

We'll also add a short escalation step: if the parties disagree about scope within 48 hours, the party seeking preservation may file the emergency petition. The petition is limited to preservation measures and account suspension.

If this aligns with NovaWorks, we'll circulate the single tracked-change MSA by EOD tomorrow. Once language is agreed, we can add the playbook excerpt to the SOW appendix for operational runbooks.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
